title: Conversation Tiling: runtime design notes
content:
Purpose:
This is an informal scratchpad for the "conversation tiling" idea: split long chat histories into overlapping tiles (segments) to enable efficient KV-cache reuse, incremental prefill, and cheaper recompute for long sessions. Goal is a pragmatic runtime API + local policy we can try as an experiment in Dedicated/Hosted routing.

High level problem we want to solve:
- Long sessions (10k+ tokens) are expensive to run every time a new prompt arrives.
- Full prefix caching is heavy (memory, eviction churn) and brittle as history grows.
- Need a way to: 1) cap per-request prep work, 2) reuse cached representations, 3) support partial recompute when context changes (edits, deletions, new system instructions).

Core idea:
- Partition the conversation timeline into fixed or adaptive "tiles". Each tile contains a contiguous set of messages / tokens. Tiles overlap by an overlap_ratio to preserve attention continuity across tile boundaries.
- At inference time, instead of loading the entire prefix, runtime identifies a small number of tiles that cover the needed context (e.g., last N tiles + sparse older anchors).
- Each tile has a compact prefill artifact: serialized KV cache delta, attention anchors, and a checksum/manifest.
- Prefill step is incremental: combine tile artifacts (apply in order) and then compute the final prompt continuation with a short local prefix.

Advantages:
- Memory bounded by tile cache (LRU at tile granularity).
- Prefill cost proportional to number of tiles (configurable), so we can enforce per-request CPU/GPU bounds.
- Easier invalidation: when a message edits, only tiles overlapping that range need recompute.
- Better multi-tenant fairness: tile size and burst budgets can be enforced per-tenant.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Tile size and overlap: fixed tokens (e.g., 1024) vs message-aware boundaries. Small tiles => more ops + more metadata overhead; large tiles => heavier recompute on small edits.
- Overlap_ratio between 5% and 30%—needs microbench. Overlap reduces boundary artifacts but increases storage and prefill cost.
- When to compact: merge adjacent cold tiles into an anchor-only tile (no KV cache, only condensate embeddings).
- How to handle system prompt edits and instruction injection (applies globally). Option: maintain a separate top-level tile for immutable system instructions and always apply first.

API surface (sketch) - runtime-facing endpoints and shapes:
1) Tile store API (internal runtime service)
- GET /internal/v1/tiles/{tenant}/{tile_id} -> {tile_manifest, kv_blob_id, token_span}
- POST /internal/v1/tiles/{tenant} body={start_token, end_token, overlap_left, overlap_right, reason} -> {tile_id, manifest}
- PATCH /internal/v1/tiles/{tenant}/{tile_id}?recompute=true -> triggers background recompute

2) Inference prefill hook (exposed in the request path)
- When an incoming request arrives the runtime calls the tiler to resolve which tile_ids to apply.
- Example payload (pseudo-JSON):
  {
    "tenant_id": "acct-12",
    "session_id": "s-9a2b",
    "cursor_token_index": 12345,
    "target_lookback_tokens": 3072,
    "max_tiles": 4,
    "policy": "latency_preferred" // or cost_preferred
  }
- Response: {ordered_tile_ids: ["t-101","t-102"], prefill_plan: [{tile_id, apply_order, kv_blob}]}

3) Client-visible knobs (config snippets):
- session.tiling.enabled: boolean (default: true for long sessions)
- session.tiling.tile_size_tokens: int (example default 2048)
- session.tiling.overlap_tokens: int or ratio (default 128 or 6%)
- session.tiling.max_prefill_tiles: int (default 3)
- session.tiling.prefill_timeout_ms: int (deadline for applying tile prefill; fallback to cheaper plan if exceeded)
- session.tiling.expiry_policy: "ttl" | "lru" | "pinned"

Prefill plan heuristics (runtime):
- Prefer most recent tiles covering the prompt cursor. If lookback budget exhausted, include sparse anchors (one every K tiles) to preserve long-range coherence.
- If prefill_timeout_ms expires, fallback to: a) token-only precompute (embeddings or condensed summary), or b) call without prefill (last-resort).
- Cost-aware policy: if tenant has low budget, reduce max_prefill_tiles or increase overlap to favor accuracy per tile.

Tile manifest contents (compact):
- tile_id
- start_token_index, end_token_index, approx_message_range
- content_hash
- kv_blob_id (pointer to blobstore or object store)
- anchors: list of attention anchors or condensed embeddings for tile start/end
- created_at, last_recomputed_at, recompute_reason

On-disk / blobstore format:
- kv_blob: compressed binary (quantized, delta-encoded), ideally backend independent. We'll store a small JSON manifest alongside binary to allow partial reads.

ASCII system diagram (runtime view):

  [ingress] --> [router] --> [ingress-proxy] --> [tiling-resolver] --> [runtime-shard(s)]
                                              |                            |
                                              +--> [tile-store] <---------+
                                                     (blobstore + metadata)

- ingress-proxy enforces deadlines and budgets. For requests flagged as tiling-aware it asks tiling-resolver for an ordered prefill plan. The runtime shards apply tile KV blobs in order (apply sequence).

Eviction / Lifecycle:
- Tiles have a TTL and LRU score. Tenant quotas determine how many tiles can be pinned.
- Recompute happens on: message edit, message deletion, system prompt change, or periodic hygiene (staleness threshold). Recompute can be synchronous for small tiles or async for big ones (with temporary marker and degraded prefill).

Testing matrix (experiments we should run):
- Perf microbench: for model X (e.g., Llama-3-70B-8k) measure prefill latency vs tile count and tile size.
- Quality regression test: prompt suite with boundary tokens around tiles to measure drop-off in coherence.
- Edit test: measure recompute time for a single message edit in middle of long session for different tile sizes.
- Cost sim: synthetic workload mixing many short chats and few long ones; simulate tile store size and eviction churn.

Rollout plan (rudimentary):
1) Implement tile_store as an optional internal service behind a feature flag (tiling_v1).
2) Add client-side toggles in runtime config and default to off for small tenants.
3) Run canary for few tenants with long-session workloads. Collect metrics: prefill_latency, request_tail_latency, token-cost, cache-hit-rate, coherency-regression-score.
4) Iterate on overlap and default tile sizes.

Edge cases / gotchas:
- Cross-tenant dedupe: cannot share KV blobs across tenants unless encrypted multi-tenant format is used.
- Tokenization drift: if tokenizer version changes, tile token indexes become invalid. Need tokenizer-version in manifest.
- Model variant compatibility: tile KV blobs bound to model version/quant/profile. Keep manifest model_version and quant_profile; resolve to compatible fallback.
- Tool-calls or function-calls inside messages: they are part of tile content; edits that change tool-call signature may require broader recompute. Mark tiles containing tool-call stubs as high-cost to recompute.

Developer TODOs (short):
- [ ] Prototype tile manifest + small test harness for Llama family (Benji)
- [ ] Add tiling-resolver RPC and default heuristics (Aisha)
- [ ] Simulate eviction behavior and run cost sims (Marisol)
- [ ] Add tokenizer_version and model_profile into manifest schema

Notes to self:
- Keep this as a user-level experiment first (users directory scratchpad). If results look promising, formalize into an RFC that includes security/privacy considerations for Private deployments.
- Think about a summary/condensation tile (small MD summary + embeddings) rather than raw KV for very old context — cheaper to store.

References / quick links:
- JIRA-ENG-1423: conversation tiling spike
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tiler/pull/87 (prototype code)
- Confluence draft: conversation-tiling-rfc-2025

End of notes.
